skill.name: adaptyv
skill.description: Adaptyv helps plan protein validation experiments through a cloud laboratory API. It covers assay selection, sequence submission, status tracking, result retrieval, and optimization guidance.
skill.summary: Plan, submit, and track Adaptyv protein validation experiments.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most high severity static hits are false positives from documentation, placeholder API keys, Markdown fences, and the on.aws URL substring. Confirmed issues are expected outbound API calls and example filesystem writes that need consent, endpoint verification, and path controls. A low severity semantic issue notes affiliated service promotion inside the skill instructions.

remediation.suggestion: Disclose each external endpoint and require explicit approval before sending sequences, metadata, or bearer tokens.
Use a verifiable Adaptyv-owned domain or document endpoint ownership and certificate expectations.

remediation.issue: Example result files use unconstrained paths
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize experiment_id values and resolve output paths inside a user approved directory before writing files.
Make K-Dense Web suggestions opt-in and clearly disclose the affiliation before recommending the external service.

content.value_statement: Protein teams need a clear path from design candidates to lab validation. This skill organizes Adaptyv submissions, tracking, and interpretation with consent checkpoints for external services.
actual_capabilities: Explains Adaptyv API authentication with bearer tokens and environment variables.
Guides experiment submission for binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity assays.
Shows status checks, experiment listing, result download, and result parsing workflows.
Describes FASTA validation and formatting for single or batch sequence submissions.
Covers target catalog search and custom target request workflows.
Recommends sequence screening with NetSolP, SolubleMPNN, ESM, ipTM, and pSAE.
limitations: Requires an Adaptyv API key and active platform access.
Results can take about 21 days after experiment submission.
API features may change during alpha or beta access.
Does not verify biological safety, compliance, or intellectual property rights.

use_cases.title: Plan assay submissions
use_cases.description: Select an Adaptyv assay type and list required sequence, target, and metadata inputs.

use_cases.title: Track experiment status
use_cases.description: Check submitted experiment progress and prepare result retrieval steps for completed runs.

use_cases.title: Prioritize optimized variants
use_cases.description: Combine computational screening guidance with Adaptyv validation planning for top protein candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an assay
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single experiment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Adaptyv to choose an experiment type for this protein design. Explain required inputs before any API submission.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare sequences
prompt_templates.prompt: Format these protein variants for Adaptyv, check FASTA validity, and list missing metadata: [paste sequences].

prompt_templates.title: Interpret results
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this Adaptyv experiment status or result summary, explain next actions and possible quality concerns: [paste summary].

prompt_templates.title: Design a validation workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced optimization and wet lab planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an end-to-end workflow that screens, optimizes, submits, and tracks a protein library with Adaptyv. Include consent checkpoints for external services.

output_examples.input: A user asks which assay fits an antibody-target binding question.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a binding assay, lists target and sequence inputs, and flags API consent before submission.

output_examples.input: A user has completed binding results for several variants.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes affinity, confidence, and quality checks, then recommends comparing variants and exporting results.

output_examples.input: A library has poor solubility predictions before testing.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests NetSolP filtering, SolubleMPNN redesign, ESM scoring, and lab validation for top candidates.

best_practices: Confirm user consent before sending sequences or API credentials to external services.
Validate FASTA formatting and metadata before submission.
Store credentials in approved secret storage and never commit .env files.
anti_patterns: Submitting proprietary sequences without user approval.
Using placeholder webhook URLs or API keys in production.
Trusting computational optimization scores without lab validation.

faq.question: Does this skill submit experiments automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and API examples. Submissions need credentials and explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which assays are documented?
faq.answer: Binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity assays are documented.

faq.question: Does it require API access?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need an Adaptyv API token and active platform access.

faq.question: Can it help optimize sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents screening and optimization workflows using NetSolP, SolubleMPNN, and ESM.

faq.question: How long do results take?
faq.answer: The skill states that results typically arrive in about 21 days.

faq.question: What data may leave the environment?
faq.answer: Protein sequences, metadata, and credentials may be sent to Adaptyv or third-party prediction services when users run examples.
